text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike detected - inference-api-5xx-rate > 2% (rolling 5m) - 37 events - dedupe_key=svc/inference/5xx

pagerduty: PagerDuty: page fired to @devon_oncall (primary) and @maria_ops (escalation). Incident ID: PD-98431

devon_oncall: acking on behalf of me, pulling graphs now. any customer-facing errors reported?

support_jade: saw 3 support tickets referencing 502s from integrations-labs this morning, they're all still open.

alex_chu: looks like a rollout hit the inference runtime autoscaler around 00:12 UTC, saw increased queue time + 5xx surge in logs. tagging @paul_engineer

paul_engineer: on it. grabbing logs and tailing the replica pods. suspecting a bad kernel selection combo after the new runtime patch.

devon_oncall: incident-bot, can we group/suppress duplicates? we're getting a paging storm with many alerts for the same dedupe key.

incident-bot: ACTION: auto-grouped 42 alerts into group svc/inference/5xx (rule: dedupe_key). Suppression suggestion: create a temporary silence to avoid further paging storms. Reason: rapid spike correlated with deployment artifact "runtime-v3.4.1".

maria_ops: +1 to silence while we triage. propose 30m silence for alerts with dedupe_key=svc/inference/5xx, keep metric retention for analysis.

devon_oncall: creating silence now via oncall toolkit.

devon_oncall: /incident silence --key "svc/inference/5xx" --duration 30m --owner devon_oncall --note "suppress paging while triage; will escalate if error rate stays >2%"

incident-bot: Silence created: id=SL-7721, key=svc/inference/5xx, until=1770459620 (30m). Paging suppressed for grouped alerts. Auto-notes: remember to clear if resolved early.

paul_engineer: found stacktrace from runtime -> kernel mismatch causing tokenization microtimeouts, hitting upstream NLB health checks -> 502s. Rolling back runtime-v3.4.1 to v3.4.0 on a canary subset.

alex_chu: re-routing new traffic to older model instances while rollback proceeds. latency dropped for canary nodes.

support_jade: notified the three impacted customers about 'intermittent 502s' and said we're investigating; offering ETA ~30-45m.

devon_oncall: handing off in 20m to @maria_ops. leaving notes: silence in place (SL-7721), PD incident PD-98431, rollback in progress, monitoring error rate and 502 ticket list.

maria_ops: taking over at 00:45 UTC. will watch dashboards and update PD.

sre-bot: Metric alert: 5xx rate (svc/inference) decreased to 0.6% (5m) - below threshold.

incident-bot: GROUP UPDATE: grouped alert svc/inference/5xx now showing steady decline; 5xx count falling. Silence SL-7721 will auto-expire in 12m; consider clearing if resolved.

devon_oncall: good signal. cancelling silence early.

devon_oncall: /incident silence cancel SL-7721 --owner devon_oncall --note "issue mitigated by rollback, un-silencing to allow normal paging"

incident-bot: Silence SL-7721 canceled by devon_oncall. Paging restored.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: PD-98431 status: acknowledged -> resolved. Final escalation: none.

maria_ops: I'm pinging the customers with an update: issue mitigated, we rolled back runtime patch, following up with postmortem.

paul_engineer: will open a changelog/PR to revert kernel selection logic and add a canary gating check to runtime rollout playbook.

devon_oncall: quick notes for postmortem: 1) auto-grouping helped avoid N pages; 2) silence worked as intended but must ensure silences are visible to support teams; 3) add dedupe-key whitelist for customer-impacting alerts to never suppress until ack by human if severity=critical.

alex_chu: agree. also add a runbook step: when dedupe_key matches deployment artifact, automatically annotate PD with deployment id and recent rollouts.

support_jade: copying customer ticket numbers into PD incident for audit.

maria_ops: closing loop: will run postmortem draft tomorrow and assign action items. thanks all. :thumbsup:

paul_engineer: closing logs and will push fix branch.

incident-bot: Incident PD-98431 marked resolved at 1770457850. If any workflow items remain, create a follow-up thread in #postmortems.
